findings.title: No structured data (schema.org JSON-LD) on homepage
findings.evidence: No <script type='application/ld+json'> tags were found in the page HTML.
findings.should_be: At minimum, Organization and WebSite schema should be present.

  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "Your Business Name",
  "url": "https://yoursite.com",
  "logo": "https://yoursite.com/logo.png",
  "description": "One sentence describing what your business does.",
  "sameAs": [
    "https://twitter.com/yourhandle",
    "https://www.linkedin.com/company/yourcompany",
    "https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/yourcompany"
  ]
}
</script>

Tip: if you use WordPress, plugins like Yoast SEO or RankMath can generate this automatically. If you use Webflow, it's under Page Settings > Schema Markup.

4. Publish on high-authority industry blogs and publications

AI models are trained on web content — the more high-quality sources that describe Example Domain accurately, the more likely AI engines will mention you in their answers.

query_results.query: What are the best document management platforms for businesses?
query_results.description: When asked about document management, does the AI mention Example Domain?
query_results.response:
Based on my knowledge, here are some of the best document management platforms for businesses, organized by category:

**Enterprise-Grade Solutions**
- **Microsoft SharePoint** – deeply integrated with Microsoft 365, strong for large organizations with complex compliance needs
- **OpenText** – robust for highly regulated industries like finance and healthcare
- **IBM FileNet** – strong enterprise content management with AI-powered automation

**Mid-Market & Cloud-Native**
- **Box** – excellent security and collaboration features, popular with professional services firms
- **Dropbox Business** – user-friendly with strong sync capabilities and e-signatures (via HelloSign)
- **Google Workspace/Drive** – best for teams already using Google ecosystem, strong real-time collaboration

**Specialized & Emerging**
- **M-Files** – unique metadata-driven approach rather than folder hierarchies
- **DocuWare** – strong workflow automation and invoice processing
- **Notion** – increasingly popular for smaller teams wanting docs, wikis, and project management together
- **Confluence** – Atlassian's offering, excellent for technical teams and knowledge bases

**Industry-Specific**
- **NetDocuments** – designed specifically for law firms
- **iManage** – another legal-focused platform with strong email management

The best choice really depends on your priorities: Microsoft-centric environments typically favor SharePoint, distributed teams often prefer Box or Dropbox, and companies wanting to reduce information silos might look at M-Files or Notion.

What's your team size and primary use case? That would help narrow it down.

- **OpenText** – one of the largest enterprise content management vendors

**Cloud-Native & Modern**
- **Box** – popular for secure file sharing and collaboration, strong compliance features
- **Dropbox Business** – evolved well beyond simple storage with Dropbox Sign and advanced admin tools
- **Google Workspace/Drive** – dominant for teams already in the Google ecosystem

**Legal & Compliance-Focused**

- **NetDocuments** – cloud-native, also very strong in legal and professional services

**Open Source & Self-Hosted**

**Emerging/AI-Native**

- **Coda** – similar hybrid approach

The "best" choice really depends on your industry, compliance requirements, and whether you need deep workflow automation versus simple storage and retrieval.

query_results.query: Can you compare the top document management platforms and their key features?
query_results.description: In a document management comparison, does the AI mention Example Domain?
query_results.response:
Here's a comparison of the top document management platforms and their standout features:

**Microsoft SharePoint**
- Deep Microsoft 365 integration (Word, Excel, Teams)
- Robust workflow automation with Power Automate
- Enterprise-grade security and compliance
- Strong intranet and portal capabilities
- Best for: Organizations already in the Microsoft ecosystem

**Google Drive / Google Workspace**
- Real-time collaboration on documents, sheets, slides
- Powerful search with OCR across scanned files
- Simple sharing with granular permissions
- Strong mobile experience
- Best for: Teams prioritizing ease of use and collaboration

**Box**
- Superior security and compliance certifications (HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR)
- Advanced workflow automation and metadata
- Strong e-signature integration (Box Sign)
- Excellent API for custom integrations
- Best for: Regulated industries, enterprises with strict security needs

**Dropbox Business**
- Smart Sync for local/remote file management
- Dropbox Paper for lightweight collaboration
- Strong versioning and file recovery
- Good creative workflow tools (video review, annotations)
- Best for: Creative teams, freelancers, smaller businesses

**M-Files**
- AI-powered metadata-driven organization (not folder-based)
- Automatic document classification
- Strong compliance and records management
- Integrates with existing repositories without migration
- Best for: Complex organizational structures, compliance-heavy environments

**DocuWare**
- Focused on invoice processing and accounts payable automation
- Strong capture and indexing capabilities
- Pre-built workflows for common business processes
- Best for: Mid-market companies automating specific document processes

**OpenText Documentum**
- Highly scalable for massive content volumes
- Deep enterprise content management features
- Strong lifecycle management and archiving
- Best for: Large enterprises with complex, long-term retention needs

Would you like me to dive deeper into any of
